BREAKING:  James Cody Bryant, a trans male from Bellingham, WA, was indicted today by a grand jury sitting in the Western District of Washington for conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country for Bryant’s role in a February 10, 2026, school shooting in BC, Canada. 

Bryant was in frequent communication with Tumbler Ridge trans school shooter Jesse Van Rootselaar in the six months leading up to the school shooting that killed six people and seriously injured others. Bryant is scheduled for arraignment on October 22, 2026.

The indictment details several overt acts that Bryant took to further the school shooting conspiracy:

-As early as August 2025, Bryant agreed to record the shooting and broadcast it over the internet;
-In August 2025, Bryant tested the quality of the live stream and confirmed it looked “solid.”
-At various times, Bryant offered the shooter advice on where to attack and what weapons to carry.
-In January 2026, Bryant again tested the livestream and told Van Rootselaar it worked;
-In late January, Bryant sent Van Rootselaar money via PayPal to purchase a lighter for use in an improvised explosive device

According to the RCMP, Van Rootselaar was born a male. Van Rootselaar had been transitioning and identified as female on official government identification and on law enforcement reports.

On February 10, 2026, Jesse Van Rootselaar killed two relatives and then drove to the Tumbler Ridge Secondary School where Van Rootselaar shot and killed five children ages 12 and 13 and killed an educational assistant. Van Rootselaar used an improvised explosive device to damage the school and tried to get into other classrooms by firing through locked doors. Van Rootselaar exchanged gunfire with police and ultimately committed suicide.

According to records filed in the case, shortly after the shooting, law enforcement learned Van Rootselaar had been in frequent communication with someone via the platform Discord. That person was identified as Bryant.  Law enforcement has obtained and reviewed thousands of communications between the two.

Conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country is punishable by up to life in prison.

On the day of the murders, Bryant confirmed the livestream was visible, and later that the livestream had gone down.

On various occasions, Bryant made clear the planning of the attack was illegal, discussing ways they should conceal their communications or the source of the livestream.

text:
AMERICA'S MIDTERM ELECTIONS: TRUMP IS LOSING CONTROL OF CONGRESS

With less than three weeks until the US midterm elections on 3 November, the political winds are blowing strongly against President Donald Trump and the Republicans.

And the consequences will extend far beyond Washington...

📊 WHAT ARE THE FORECASTS SAYING?

Prediction markets currently estimate:

🔵 91% probability of Democrats winning the House of Representatives.

🔵 64% probability of Democrats winning the Senate.

🔵 63% probability of Democrats controlling BOTH chambers.

The respected Cook Political Report has also shifted numerous House races towards the Democrats, while polling-based and academic forecasts broadly agree that Republicans face a difficult election.

These aren't certainties. But the direction is unmistakable.

WHAT WOULD A DEMOCRATIC SWEEP MEAN?

If Democrats win both chambers, Trump could face two years of legislative paralysis.

❌ Major tax, spending and legislative reforms would become much harder to enact.

🔎 Congressional investigations, subpoenas and oversight of the Trump administration could intensify dramatically.

⚖️ Judicial appointments and senior administration confirmations could face significant obstacles.

💰 Budget negotiations could become increasingly confrontational, raising the prospect of further government shutdowns.

Donald Trump would retain considerable executive authority, particularly over foreign policy, regulation and immigration. But his freedom to legislate would be severely constrained.

📉 WHY ARE REPUBLICANS STRUGGLING?

Cost-of-living pressures, economic uncertainty, tariffs, the conflict with Iran and dissatisfaction with Trump's leadership are weighing heavily on Republican prospects. Trump himself suffers disapproval from 23% more respondents, over his approval rating (60% vs 37%).

History also matters: the president's party frequently suffers losses in midterm elections.

🌎 WHAT ABOUT THE REST OF THE WORLD?

A Democratic Congress could challenge Trump's trade policies, scrutinise his approach to Russia, Ukraine and the Middle East (including Iran), demand greater accountability over military operations and complicate his international agenda.

For Europe and America's other allies, this could mean greater congressional checks on Washington's decisions; but also more political uncertainty.

Government bond yields in the United States have recently been at 24-year highs. Markets could react sharply and negatively, particularly if investors anticipate legislative gridlock, increased regulation or changes in fiscal policy.

🗳️ AND THE 2028 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION?

A Democratic victory would give the opposition momentum, visibility and institutional power heading towards 2028.

It could weaken Trump's political authority, intensify Republican debates about succession and complicate the ambitions of Vice President JD Vance and other potential Republican presidential candidates.

But Democrats would face their own test: can they offer a convincing alternative, rather than simply opposing Trump?

A Republican defeat in November would not automatically produce a Democratic president in 2028, but a switch is becoming much more likely. Betting markets show that the next Presidential race is wide open with JD Vance, AOC, Jon Ossoff, Gavin Newsom, and Marco Rubio in contention (and the Democrats are strongly favoured to win the next Presidency).

OVERALL ASSESSMENT

The most likely outcome is Democratic control of the House. The Senate remains more competitive, although betting markets now favour a Democratic victory there too...

A Democratic sweep would represent a major setback for Trump, likely transforming the final two years of his presidency into an extended struggle between the White House and Congress.

But gridlock isn't necessarily good governance. America needs effective institutions, responsible leadership, economic opportunity and a political system capable of delivering results.

The stakes are enormous for Americans, for the Western alliance, and for the wider world...

text:
Daniela, you accuse me of failing to see the bigger picture, then write “Be it sold or with ‘perpetuity’”. Do you actually understand the difference between selling sovereign territory and granting military access? They’re not remotely the same thing.

So which are you defending?

If it’s a sale, why is surrendering British territory to America patriotic, but surrendering it to Mauritius treachery? Does British sovereignty suddenly stop mattering when Trump is involved?

If it’s indefinite access, America already operates Diego Garcia. How does extending that access extinguish Mauritius’s legal claim? How does it remove the financial burden you confidently claim disappears? Where are the figures, the agreements or even a credible explanation?

And who exactly is this “enemy” you’re talking about? Mauritius? On what evidence?

Farage told Parliament in February 2025 that Britain should sell the islands to America if sovereignty was going to be surrendered. Now he’s talking about permanent access in exchange for Trump keeping quiet about the Falklands.

Why should a prospective British Prime Minister have to bargain with an American president over another piece of British territory? Since when was respecting British sovereignty something we had to purchase from Washington?

You’ve offered no legal argument, no financial evidence and no explanation of how your proposal works. Just blind faith that Farage must be right.

So please, Daniela, explain this bigger picture you keep mentioning. Because at present it looks remarkably like you’ve confused patriotism with doing whatever Donald Trump wants.

📱 Global Smartphone Sales Plunge 20% as Memory Chip Shortage Drives Prices Higher

📉 Historic Collapse in Smartphone Sales: Global smartphone sales reportedly plunged 20% in the third quarter of 2026, marking the weakest third quarter in 14 years. The sharp decline highlights growing pressure on the smartphone industry as rising manufacturing costs and weakening consumer demand disrupt the market.

💾 Memory Chip Shortage Disrupts Production: An ongoing shortage of memory chips is squeezing smartphone manufacturers, driving up production costs and limiting their ability to offer competitively priced devices. Strong demand for memory used in artificial intelligence infrastructure is contributing to pressure on global chip supplies.

💰 Smartphone Prices Surge 20%: Phone prices have reportedly climbed approximately 20%, making new devices increasingly expensive for consumers. Manufacturers face difficult decisions about absorbing higher component costs or passing those increases directly to buyers.

📱 Consumers Keep Their Phones Longer: Rather than upgrading to newer models, consumers are increasingly extending the lifespan of their existing smartphones. Higher prices, economic uncertainty, and relatively modest improvements between device generations are reducing incentives to replace functioning devices.

🏭 Major Smartphone Manufacturers Face Pressure: Companies including Apple, Samsung, and Xiaomi face challenges from rising component costs and weaker replacement demand. Manufacturers targeting budget conscious consumers could be particularly vulnerable because their customers are more sensitive to price increases.

🤖 AI Boom Creates Unexpected Consequences: Rapid expansion of artificial intelligence data centers is intensifying competition for semiconductor manufacturing capacity. As memory producers prioritize more profitable AI infrastructure products, consumer electronics manufacturers face tighter supplies and higher costs.

🌍 Global Electronics Industry Faces Wider Risks: Prolonged memory shortages could extend beyond smartphones, affecting laptops, tablets, gaming consoles, and other electronics. Continued price increases could further weaken consumer demand and complicate the industry's recovery.

📊 Recovery Depends on Chip Supply and Affordability: A sustained rebound in smartphone sales will likely depend on improved memory availability, stabilization of component prices, and renewed consumer willingness to upgrade. Until those conditions improve, manufacturers could face continued pressure on sales volumes and profitability.

text:
Yesterday, The Washington Post published an opinion piece by David Ignatius  It is essentially being called a leak of the American negotiating team's "peace plan." If that is true, I'm having a sense of déjà vu. It feels as though President Trump’s negotiators didn't even bother to come up with anything on their own and simply asked Russians to bail them out with ideas for the peace plan.

I tried to find at least some differences from what Russia has been demanding for years, but I couldn't find any.

President Trump's team is proposing that Ukraine give up the territories seized by Moscow. From Kushner and Witkoff's perspective, this is what a compromise looks like. The only thing that's hard to understand is where exactly the compromise is.

The EU is in shock over how two negotiating geniuses agreed to reshape the European security architecture as if they are the ones actually calling the shots there.

In 2008-2009, Moscow was pushing for a treaty that would allow it to control the security decisions of European states. In 2021, it demanded a limit on NATO expansion and a rollback of the Alliance's military presence to its 1997 levels.

Now the American team is including agreements between Europe and Russia on Russia's "security concerns" in its proposals to end the war. Truly, why didn't anyone think of this before?!

Now, about guarantees... I’m just tired... This is like an endless Budapest Memorandum...

But I think I’ve figured out where Russia's compromise is: in exchange for territorial concessions from Ukraine and the restructuring of European security, Russia will generously agree to Ukraine stopping its strikes on Russian oil refineries, while Europe gets hooked on gas again.

And Russia still needs to be persuaded to agree to all this. Here, Kushner and Witkoff propose appeasing Putin by lifting sanctions. I think that’s not enough. They should have also offered Moscow compensation for losses.

Ukraine's reconstruction is being used as an argument in favor of territorial concessions. Investment, along with the participation of the World Bank and BlackRock, is supposed to make the deal more attractive to Kyiv. Seems like someone is missing here - Gazprom, the Rotenberg brothers... Who else?

Seriously, though, it’s all depressing. It’s clear that Ukraine and Europe are being treated here not just as fools, but as some kind of pie that it’s time to divide.

If we're going to be this cynical, I'd like to ask the brilliant American team - what part of this pie is left for the United States? Right now it looks like just the wrapper.

Reports about the possible sale of Lukoil's international assets, worth approximately $20 billion, mention investors linked to business partners of Kushner and Witkoff.

Russian television is filled with such loud laughter and mockery of the American president that only someone completely isolated from reality could fail to hear it.

text:
Newspapers, television networks, research centers affiliated with the United States, and other media outlets serving its allies in the region are attempting to distort the image of Yemen and the Yemeni people in the eyes of the world. They portray Yemen, under the leadership of the Sana’a government, as having supported Gaza merely to gain domestic and regional popular support, only to pursue its destructive and destabilizing projects across the region in service of Iran once that objective had been achieved including targeting Saudi Arabia and closing the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
I have noticed this misleading narrative, saturated with fallacies, lies, and deception, circulating widely enough to warrant clarification and a reminder of the following:

• In 2015, Saudi Arabia announced the formation of an international coalition and launched its military operations against Yemen from Washington, D.C.

• The United States supported and armed this coalition and participated in its operations throughout the years of aggression and blockade against Yemen.

• Since 2015, the Saudi-led coalition has blockaded Yemen, starved its people, and killed Yemeni civilians. These actions continue to this day.

• Yemen resisted with steadfastness and courage, standing alone against massive international coalitions, without the participation or support of any foreign country.

• In 2023, Yemen supported Gaza despite still being under the Saudi-led blockade.

• Saudi Arabia intercepted several missiles and drones launched from Yemen toward Israel, thereby supporting and protecting those responsible for killing women and children in Gaza.

• Yemen targeted Israeli ships in an attempt to exert pressure and lift the blockade on the people of Gaza while they were dying of hunger.

• Saudi Arabia and the UAE established a land corridor to ensure the delivery of goods to Israel, attempting to break Yemen’s blockade of Israel.

Dutchess #IR1490 knows what it means to have a home and someone to love. Rescued from Antigua in October 2023, this beautiful 3-year-old Ridgeback mix was adopted almost immediately at one of our Mobile Adoption Events. She spent nearly three wonderful years with her person before unexpected housing circumstances brought her back into our care.

Now, Dutchess is adjusting to a big change she never expected. While she waits for a new family, we're getting to know the sweet, affectionate girl who has so much love left to give. ❤️

Dutchess is housebroken, crate-trained, LOVES people, and has enjoyed the company of other dogs. She can be a little shy when meeting someone new, but give her time to feel comfortable and you'll see her loving personality shine. A meet-and-greet is recommended for any potential canine siblings.

She's looking for an experienced home with children over 8 who will respect her gentle nature. A quieter neighborhood would be ideal, giving Dutchess the chance to settle in, feel secure, and enjoy all the comforts of home again.

text:
TRUMP HAS CHOSEN PUTIN. THE WORLD MUST FACE THE CONSEQUENCES.

Over the past 72 hours, Donald Trump has abandoned all pretenses, overturned two decades of American policy, and undermined 18 months of his own diplomacy.

He lifted sanctions on Russian diesel imports, threatened to cut intelligence sharing with Ukraine unless Kyiv stopped attacking Russian oil refineries, and demanded that Ukraine surrender one of its most effective weapons without demanding anything from Moscow in return.

He failed to condemn Russian attacks on Ukrainian power plants, including facilities owned by American companies. He expressed no sympathy for Ukrainian children killed by Russian bombs.

Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” that surprised Ukraine and was immediately violated by Russia. He blamed Kyiv for obstructing negotiations, although Ukraine repeatedly offered ceasefires while Moscow refused meaningful talks.

He portrayed Ukraine's democratically elected president as an obstacle to peace, yet maintained friendly conversations with Vladimir Putin — the one man who could end this war by ordering his troops to stop fighting.

Ukraine cannot simply stop defending itself. Capitulation would mean occupation, repression, murdered leaders, abducted children, and imprisonment. If Trump understands this, then he simply does not care.

Trump claims his policy will lower fuel prices for Americans. But Russian diesel exports cannot significantly change global prices. The current energy crisis is driven by the war with Iran, not Ukraine.

What we are witnessing looks more like a desperate attempt to force Ukraine into submission while rescuing Russia's economy.

Meanwhile, commercial negotiations involving Russian energy assets, Arctic resources, frozen funds, and potentially lucrative deals continue. The New York Times reported discussions involving Lukoil assets and business partners connected to Trump's negotiators, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. There is no evidence that either man would personally profit.

The message to Moscow is unmistakable: keep fighting, because Washington may eventually offer you something valuable.

Europe must now accept three painful lessons.

First, America under Trump is no longer a reliable ally. Decades of foreign policy can be overturned overnight by one man's impulses.

Second, dictators appear to receive better treatment in Trump's Washington than democratically elected leaders. Canada is a far more dependable energy partner than Russia, yet Trump listens to Moscow while alienating Ottawa, Berlin, and London.

Third, this administration appears willing to put commercial opportunities ahead of longstanding security commitments.

Fortunately, democratic nations can cooperate without the American president. Ukraine will continue fighting with European intelligence, German weapons, French support, and substantial assistance from Scandinavia, Poland, and other allies.

Europe, Canada, and democratic nations across the Pacific must strengthen their economic and security partnerships.

Trump's relationship with Russia remains extraordinarily strange. Since his first Moscow visit in 1987, he has repeatedly echoed Russian positions while attacking America's democratic alliances. His opinions on countless issues have changed, but this preference has remained remarkably consistent.

Yet Trump does not speak for every American. Members of Congress from both parties have challenged his Russian diesel policy.

And General Alexus Grynkewich, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe, delivered a very different message in Warsaw: any attack on NATO would face a devastating response against the forces and infrastructure supporting the aggression.

Such clarity from the White House could help deter Russian attacks, sabotage, and further escalation.

But Trump refuses to speak that language.

The world must prepare for the possibility that he never will.

Adapted from Anne Applebaum, The Atlantic, October 12, 2026.

Oh yeah, no, that’s the other half of the story: exercise. I was an athlete in school, so I did conditioning for my sports and was in good shape. That said, I also started smoking to be cool when I was about 15.

After high school, I didn’t go to college. Nobody had raised me with the expectation that I would. My father offered at the very end, but it felt so random because it had never really been part of the plan. Once I was out of school, organized sports disappeared from my life, and I never really got back into athletics.

I was fine weight-wise until I had my first kid. I gained 60 pounds—30 of them in the first four months, when you’re not even showing yet. So that was exciting. I eventually lost about half of it and felt somewhat decent. Then I decided to have another baby 12 years later, and the same thing happened again.

The problem is that I hurt everywhere, from my neck down to my ankles. There’s always something that feels bruised or injured, sometimes with sharp pain. What hurts the most depends on what I’m doing. If I’m sitting and working on data, it’s my upper back, neck, and arms. If I’m standing, it’s my back, ankles, and knees. All of this started before the weight gain, but it makes high-impact exercise very difficult.

What works best for me is a pool. I did pool exercises years ago, and that was great. With other workouts, I can sometimes get through them, but then I wake up the next day hurting so badly that I can’t do it again for four days. It’s hard to sustain a routine that way.

Pool exercise is really what I need to get back into. I just don’t have the bandwidth right now. My son only attends school for a few hours a day, with both drop-off and pickup in the middle of the workday, and I’m trying to manage my work around all of that too. Swimming would be ideal, but my issues are also very bad in my arms. At all times my arms are sore to the touch- like pressing a bruise and my biceps and triceps achy have tears- like it feels like a ripped muscle. So that’s where I’m at. I walk and bike daily though

text:
Agreed. And oh my god, yes — Alan Wake II is incredibly well-crafted, from its visuals to its rich, multi-layered narrative. It’s truly the kind of game that leaves you with a lingering, pleasant aftertaste. For me, First Light provided that same kind of lasting impression this year — I hadn’t expected to enjoy it nearly as much as I did. 

Requiem is great for the first few hours — the segments with Grace — but as things unfold, you start to realize just how bare-bones the game actually is, in more ways than one. While I could forgive the lack of solid puzzles during Grace’s chapters (though they did try with that vending machine, lol), the fact that Leon’s sections just recycle the same enemies over and over really killed it for me. The only moments in Leon’s parts that actually gave me a "wow" factor were the shootout in the glass high-rise and the motorcycle chase — though, by my second playthrough, that sequence had completely lost its charm. 

Honestly, I just don’t get the hype surrounding RE9. It’s not a bad game, but it’s far from perfect; it doesn’t offer any fresh gameplay mechanics or a particularly deep story. 

It’s highly likely that the "Leon effect" is at play here.

text:
Your next client might send an AI agent first.

Your next customer could be someone browsing your website, or an AI agent researching businesses on their behalf.

I’ve worked on a few local business websites, and I’m surprised how often the basics are buried under fancy design and vague copy.

1. Say what you actually do.

“We provide innovative financial solutions” could describe a thousand businesses.

“Monthly bookkeeping and QuickBooks cleanup for small businesses in Charlotte” tells me who you help and what you offer.

2. Make your pricing and services clear.

Would someone know what they’re getting before contacting you?

You don’t need to publish every price. Even a starting rate, what’s included, or a simple explanation of how quotes work helps people figure out if you’re a good fit.

3. Make the next step obvious.

Open your website on your phone.

How long does it take to find your services, book a call, or request a quote?

People are already using AI to research businesses. As AI agents start doing more of that research, the information on your website will matter even more.

Make it easy for someone to understand what you do, who you help, and how to hire you.

Your next customer might never even visit your homepage.

text:
If This Is a Simulation and These Texts Are Its Owner's Manual, Then No Wonder Everything Is All Fucked Up and Shit

Buried in the fifteenth chapter of the Book of Jubilees, in the middle of a passage about circumcision that nobody reads, sits a sentence that ought to come with a warning label. The nations are many, it says, and they all belong to God, "and over all hath He placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from Him." Then it slams the door: "But over Israel He did not appoint any angel or spirit, for He alone is their ruler."

That's R. H. Charles's translation from the Ge'ez, made in the early 1900s. Read it twice. The peoples of the earth were handed out to heavenly managers, and the managers were given a brief. The brief was misdirection.

Plenty of cultures have stories about beings above humanity who teach it, rule it, rebel and get chained. What's rare is a text that says the rulers were posted over the nations on purpose, with leading astray in the job description.

The Watchers are the classic case. Their book, 1 Enoch, survives complete only in Ge'ez, as scripture for the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo church and the Beta Israel; Aramaic fragments turned up among the Dead Sea Scrolls. Its premise in one line: two hundred of them came down on Mount Hermon, swore an oath together and taught humanity what it wasn't supposed to know.

Then Deuteronomy 32 draws the map. When the Most High divided the nations, he set their borders by the number of the sons of God, in the Dead Sea Scroll reading that the ESV and NRSV print. The next verse is the hinge: "For the LORD's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance." The nations go to the sons of God. One people is held back.

Later tradition ties the carving to Babel: seventy nations, seventy languages, everybody scattered and handed to lesser gods who then went bad. Confusing the languages is the cheapest wall there is for anyone who wants people kept apart.

And from inside any one flock, the other flocks' shepherds look like demons. In Sanskrit a deva is a god; in Avestan a daeva is a demon. Same word, opposite sides of a border.

The reading says religions work, in the record's own words, as dividing tools: each nation its cult, each cult its overseer, each set of worshippers taught that the other overseers are demons. The shepherds hold the leash. The flocks just get walked.

Read it as the manual, as a working frame and nothing more, and the first chapter is a network diagram. The Watchers are the admins. Each partition gets its own login screen, its own language pack and its own warning that every other partition is malware.

The modern vocabulary came from a computer scientist.

Jacques Vallée spent decades studying UFO reports and the belief movements around them. In The Invisible College, in 1975, he concluded the phenomenon pointed to "a control system." In Dimensions, in 1988, he called it "a spiritual control system for human consciousness."

Vallée meant regulation, belief steered over centuries like a thermostat. He never said the system built religions as walls between peoples; that's this essay's extension. John Keel argued the same intelligences posed as gods, angels and demons, dressing for each era.

Now run it through the simulation frame, as a working frame and nothing more. A system that has to keep a huge population from converging would split it into partitions, each with a local administrator, its own rulebook, its own language and its own story about the other administrators. The partition is visible in the documents. The partitioner isn't. In the manual's own terms, the admin layer is written in and the architect is left out.

There's a strong objection, and it deserves its full weight.

Every one of these texts exempts its own people. Deuteronomy keeps Jacob for the LORD. Jubilees says no angel rules Israel at all. Every ancient city said the same: Marduk had Babylon, Chemosh had Moab. Scholars read the allotment as geopolitics with a heavenly seal, and cognitive scientists say human brains would fill the sky with watchers whether or not anyone was there.

So the version where the overseers sit above all religions, including the ones claiming exemption, is not in the texts. It's speculation.

But try it on. A flock told it alone has no shepherd but God will never compare its shepherd with anyone else's. Each tradition then describes the arrangement accurately for everybody except itself, which is exactly what a well-run partition would produce. Inside the frame, it's a design feature: an exemption clause in every partition's firmware.

Now strip off the robes and say it the way it would be said at a bar.

The old books describe a world chopped up on purpose. Every people gets a boss. Every boss gets a rulebook, a language and a story about why the people next door are going to hell. At least one of those books says outright that the bosses were put there to lead people astray. If this is a simulation and these texts are its owner's manual, then no wonder everything is all fucked up and shit. It was designed to be this way. No wonder everybody hates their government. The thing was never built to run well. It was built to keep the flocks apart and the shepherds in charge, and by that standard it runs like a Swiss watch.

Check the scoreboard. Politicians promise one thing and do the opposite so routinely that the lie is part of the ceremony.

On October 21, 1964, Lyndon Johnson promised not to send "American boys nine or ten thousand miles away from home." By the end of 1968 more than half a million were in Vietnam. On August 18, 1988, George H. W. Bush said "Read my lips: no new taxes," and in 1990 signed a budget that raised them. On October 11, 2000, George W. Bush wanted a "humble" foreign policy; within three years the country occupied Afghanistan and Iraq. Barack Obama ordered Guantánamo closed in 2009. It's still open. In June 2024 Joe Biden said he wouldn't pardon his son. On December 1, 2024, he did.

Seven presidents, both parties, one pattern. And it's not just American. Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index for 2025, published February 10, 2026, put the global average at 42 out of 100; 122 of 182 countries scored below 50, and the United States hit 64, its lowest ever. Read as the manual at work, the presidents aren't bugs. They're partition admins doing what the rulebook rewards: promise the flock one thing, deliver the system another. It runs the same in every partition, which is what a shared operating system looks like.

Then comes the part polite essays skip.

Every one of these texts carves out an exception for the chosen. Take it literally, and the tradition itself says what direct rule from God costs. Amos put it in one sentence: "You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities." Chosen, in the oldest reading, isn't a shield. It's a higher standard and a closer audit.

Now hold that verse up to the faction that turned "chosen" into "superior," and the government that handed it power. The ordinary people of any country are not its elites, and the bill below is addressed to the elites.

The record is dated and public. In 1984 the American-born rabbi Meir Kahane, whose Kach movement preached expelling Arabs, won a Knesset seat; in 1988 Israel barred his list as racist. On February 25, 1994, a Kach follower, Baruch Goldstein, killed 29 Muslim worshippers in Hebron. On July 31, 2015, Jewish extremists firebombed a home in the West Bank village of Duma, killing a toddler and both his parents.

That movement didn't stay on the fringe. In 2007 an Israeli court convicted Itamar Ben-Gvir of incitement to racism and supporting a terrorist organization, Kach. A portrait of Goldstein hung in his home until 2020. In December 2022 he became minister of national security. On February 26, 2023, settlers rampaged through the Palestinian town of Huwara; on March 1, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said Huwara should be "wiped out," by the state, then said he'd misspoken. Eighteen days later he said there was "no such thing as a Palestinian people." On November 21, 2024, the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and Yoav Gallant.

Line that up against Amos and the hypocrisy is the whole story. The faction that claims God's own portion acts as if the portion came with immunity, when its own prophet promised the opposite. In the manual's terms, this is the exemption clause executing: a faction told it has no admin above it acts as if it has no auditor either. The frame applies the same way to every partition that has claimed the same clause, and there are plenty.

Now turn the flashlight on the country that likes to call itself one nation under God.

The question goes like this: the kids recite that line every morning, half the internet swears Washington takes orders from Tel Aviv, so was America built to be the new Israel? The answer is on paper.

Start on a ship. In 1630 John Winthrop told his Puritans bound for Massachusetts Bay that "we shall be as a city upon a hill, the eyes of all people are upon us." The Puritans read their crossing as Exodus, and New England as the promised land. A people that thinks it's Israel's sequel signs up for the whole deal, the blessing and the bill.

The self-image never died. It got laminated. On June 14, 1954, Flag Day, President Eisenhower signed the law putting "under God" into the Pledge of Allegiance, a godly nation squared off against godless communism.

Then came the theology that turned the mandate into foreign policy. The 1909 Scofield Reference Bible carried Darby's dispensationalism into millions of American homes: the Jewish return to the land is a prophetic clock that has to tick before the end. Add the Genesis promise to bless whoever blesses Abraham, and backing Israel becomes a ticket to salvation. John Hagee founded Christians United for Israel on that reading in 2006; the group claims more than 10 million members.

The Christian push came first. In March 1891 a Chicago evangelist, William Blackstone, petitioned President Benjamin Harrison to help give Palestine to the Jews, six years before the first Zionist Congress. In the frame, this is a partition installing a second copy of another partition's exemption clause and wiring the two together. Two partitions, one firmware, each certain it's the one held back.

So follow the money and the names. Who sets American policy on Israel, and how, is not hidden. It's filed.

Start with the aid. On September 14, 2016, the Obama administration signed a memorandum of understanding pledging Israel $38 billion in military aid for fiscal 2019 through 2028, which the White House billed as the largest pledge of military assistance in US history. On April 24, 2024, Congress added $8.7 billion in Public Law 118-50. It's a covenant Congress keeps legislating.

Next, the election money. AIPAC's super PAC, the United Democracy Project, spent $37.86 million in independent expenditures in the 2023-24 cycle, out of $61.37 million total, by OpenSecrets' count.

In New York's 16th District it spent $9.87 million against Representative Jamaal Bowman and $4.73 million for George Latimer, about $14.6 million, the "record" The New York Times put in a headline that June. Bowman lost.

In Missouri's 1st it spent $5.24 million against Representative Cori Bush and $3.36 million for Wesley Bell, about $8.6 million. Bush lost.

Two sitting members of Congress, both critics of the war in Gaza, removed in one summer by one PAC. Every other member watched it happen. That's the lesson the money is buying.

Now the megadonors, by name.

FEC filings show Haim Saban of Saban Capital, Paul Singer of Elliott Management and Bernard Marcus, the Home Depot co-founder, each writing checks to UDP, $1 million at a time, in 2023 and 2024. Saban gives to Democrats. Singer and Marcus give to Republicans. The checks land in the same PAC.

Then the Adelsons. Sheldon Adelson met Donald Trump at Trump Tower ten days before the 2017 inauguration and came out reporting that moving the US embassy to Jerusalem would be a major priority, The New York Times reported. In December 2017 Trump recognized Jerusalem as Israel's capital. AP reported that the administration weighed Adelson's offer to pay for part of the new embassy. On May 14, 2018, Adelson sat in the audience when it opened. In March 2019 Trump recognized Israeli sovereignty over the occupied Golan Heights.

The president said it himself. On October 13, 2025, in Israel's Knesset, Trump called Miriam Adelson to her feet and said of her and her late husband: "they were very responsible for so much, including getting me thinking about the Golan Heights." He added, "She's got 60 billion in the bank," and said he once asked her whether she loved the United States or Israel more. "She refused to answer," he said. In 2024 she put $100 million into her pro-Trump super PAC, Preserve America.

The embassy, Jerusalem and the Golan: three policy wins, the donor named by the president who signed them.

Then the revolving door, which spins between the lobby, the think tanks, the government and the contractors.

Martin Indyk joined AIPAC in 1982 as deputy research director and in 1985 co-founded the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, later saying it was "very hard to get acceptances" for research "seen as coming from AIPAC." He became Bill Clinton's top Middle East adviser, served twice as US ambassador to Israel, and returned as Obama's special envoy in 2013.

Dennis Ross, a Middle East hand for four presidents, was the Washington Institute's counselor from 2001 to 2009, became Hillary Clinton's special adviser for the Gulf and Iran in February 2009, moved to the National Security Council, and went back to the institute in 2011.

David Friedman, Donald Trump's bankruptcy lawyer and president of American Friends of Beit El Yeshiva, a fundraising arm for a West Bank settlement, became US ambassador to Israel in 2017 and led the Jerusalem embassy dedication.

Lloyd Austin sat on the board of United Technologies, then Raytheon Technologies, from 2016 until January 22, 2021, the day the Senate confirmed him as secretary of defense. He ran the Pentagon through the first fifteen months of the Gaza war.

Then there's the blackmail talk, which mostly means Jeffrey Epstein. Stick to the record.

In 2019 The Wall Street Journal reported, from Epstein's own calendar, that former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak met him about 30 times between 2013 and 2017. Barak acknowledged the visits and two flights on Epstein's plane. The New York Times reported Barak got about $2.3 million from a foundation associated with Epstein, and Haaretz and released records show an Epstein trust put $1 million in 2015 into a Barak partnership that bought into the startup later renamed Carbyne.

The intelligence-asset story is a different animal. Its best-known source is a 2019 Daily Beast report quoting an anonymous former White House official, who said Alexander Acosta had been told Epstein "belonged to intelligence." Acosta denied it to House Oversight investigators in 2025. In July 2025 a Justice Department and FBI memo found no "client list" and "no credible evidence" that Epstein "blackmailed prominent individuals." The asset story is unproven and denied. Read as the manual at work, none of this needs a secret. Aid written into law, primaries priced by the race, donors credited from a parliament's floor, staff rotating from lobby to government and back: that's how a partition's admins keep each other in place. Every partition has its version. This one files paperwork.

Which brings it back to Amos. A nation that believes it's the second Israel will defend the first the way a believer defends scripture, without asking for receipts. It isn't strategy. It's faith. But Amos 3:2 doesn't offer a discount for sequels. If America claimed the covenant, it claimed the ledger too.

And it's never been one people's sickness. Being chosen is the oldest drug on the planet, and nearly every power that ever rose got hooked.

Rome had it in verse: Virgil told the Roman his art was to rule the peoples. James I told Parliament in 1610 that "kings are justly called gods." In 1845 John L. O'Sullivan gave America its "manifest destiny." Kipling sold the British "the White Man's Burden" in 1899. Imperial Japan taught a living god until the emperor renounced it on January 1, 1946. The Nuremberg Laws of September 15, 1935 wrote a master race into German statute. V. D. Savarkar's Hindutva, in 1923, defined the true nation by blood and holy land. On June 29, 2014, the Islamic State declared a caliphate and set out to exterminate the Yazidis.

Different gods, different centuries, same move. Each heard it was the portion held back and used that to justify doing to others what it would never accept done to itself. In the manual's language, that's the exemption clause shipped to every partition at once, America's included. Same firmware, different skins.

Now the modern mystery, the one that still has lawyers billing hours a quarter-century later. September 11, 2001. Stick to the paper, because the paper is strange enough.

Start with the Saudis. Fifteen of the nineteen hijackers were Saudi nationals. The 9/11 Commission found no evidence that the Saudi government as an institution, or senior officials individually, funded al-Qaeda. But 28 pages of Congress's joint inquiry about possible Saudi support stayed classified until July 15, 2016, published as leads, not vetted conclusions.

Then the FBI kept digging, under a code name: Operation Encore. Records released after President Biden's September 2021 declassification order describe "significant logistic support" to two hijackers, Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar, in Southern California. Omar al-Bayoumi, a Saudi national, co-signed their San Diego lease. Fahad al-Thumairy, an imam in Los Angeles, was an accredited Saudi diplomat, and a memo says someone was "tasked by Thumairy to assist Hazmi and Midhar." A 2017 FBI report released in 2022 says Bayoumi was paid as a "cooptee" of Saudi intelligence. The FBI's May 2021 closing memo found insufficient evidence to charge anyone. Saudi Arabia calls any allegation of complicity "categorically false."

The families sued in 2003. On August 28, 2025, Judge George B. Daniels denied Saudi Arabia's renewed motion to dismiss, without ruling on the merits. On October 7, 2026, the Second Circuit heard Saudi Arabia's appeal and took it under advisement; lawyers expect a ruling in early 2027. Nobody has been found liable. Nobody has been cleared either.

And the flights. On September 20, the so-called Bin Ladin flight left with 26 aboard, most of them relatives of Usama Bin Ladin. The 9/11 Commission found no Saudi flights left before airspace reopened on September 13 and concluded no one with known links to terrorism departed.

Now Israel. On the afternoon of September 11, New Jersey police pulled over a van belonging to Urban Moving Systems, after a caller said men had been seen celebrating as the towers burned, and arrested five young Israelis. They were held on visa violations, questioned and polygraphed. ABC News reported in 2002 that The Forward had said the FBI concluded two were Israeli intelligence operatives, which Israel denied, and that the FBI said its investigation "has not identified anybody who in this country had pre-knowledge of the events of 9/11." Per that reporting, the investigation found no evidence of foreknowledge or of any role in the attacks. After 71 days the five were deported.

Now Washington. On August 6, 2001, the President's Daily Brief carried an item titled "Bin Ladin Determined to Strike in US." The CIA had tracked al-Mihdhar and al-Hazmi to an al-Qaeda meeting in Kuala Lumpur, then lost them, and the FBI wasn't told of their US travel in time. The Commission's verdict: "a failure of imagination." In September 2000 the Project for the New American Century, whose founding statement Dick Cheney, Donald Rumsfeld and Paul Wolfowitz had signed, wrote that the military transformation it wanted "is likely to be a long one, absent some catastrophic and catalyzing event, like a new Pearl Harbor." Eighteen months after the towers fell, the country was in Baghdad.

So lay it on the table. Three governments' fingerprints on the margins of one day: Saudi officials in the hijackers' support network, Israeli nationals arrested in a moving van, an American intelligence system that had the names and the warning and sat on both. And a policy shop that had written down, a year early, what it would take to get the wars it wanted, and then got them. On paper, that's why it looks coordinated.

The official record says something narrower. Al-Qaeda planned and carried out the attacks, and no investigation found that the US or Israeli government took part. The question of Saudi officials' links is still in court, waiting on the Second Circuit.

Now put it through the frame, and label it what it is: speculation. Three partitions, one event. Two decades of war. Every flock hardened against the others. If an admin layer wanted a single partition-maintenance event, it's hard to design a better one. Were the Watchers running it? The record can't say. This essay can't either. It leaves the lock where it is.

The sky has been strange lately too, on the record.

On February 4, 2023, an F-22 shot down a Chinese surveillance balloon off South Carolina. Over the next three days the military shot down three more objects, over Alaska, the Yukon and Lake Huron; none was identified as Chinese. On July 26, 2023, former intelligence officer David Grusch told a House hearing, under oath, that the government ran secret UAP programs. The Pentagon said it found no verifiable evidence. More hearings followed on November 13, 2024, and September 9, 2025.

Nobody has shown what any of it is. But for a species that wrote down, more than two thousand years ago, that beings came down from the sky to run the partitions, it's a strange time to be looking up.

So here's the whole machine, laid out as the working frame it is and nothing more. None of it can be proven. All of it fits the record.

The allotment is the architecture: seventy-odd partitions, each with its own border, language and rulebook. The Watchers are the admins, who by the oldest manual came down on a mountain and swore an oath to one another. The exemption clause is the firmware: every partition is told it's the special one, so none ever compares its admin with anyone else's.

Everything in between reads like the system's log file. Presidents who promise peace and ship troops. A faction that reads "chosen" as "immune." A country that wrote itself in as the sequel and bankrolls the original by statute. One September morning with three partitions' names in the margins, and twenty years of war after it. Lights in the sky nobody will explain.

But the admins don't stand outside the machine. That's the part the manual is honest about. They're inside their own sandbox, bound by the architecture they run, and every text that has the scene ends in an audit: the unveiling, the judgment, the moment the logs get read aloud. Amos gave the standard for anyone who claimed the closest access: more privilege, harder account.

Against all of it stands one verse from the forty-ninth sura of the Qur'an, which keeps the map and fires the middle managers: "O humanity! Indeed, We created you from a male and a female, and made you into peoples and tribes so that you may get to know one another." Same partitions, opposite purpose.

So the questions stay open, because nothing on paper closes them. Is the partition a design or an accident? Are the Watchers running the sandbox, or just stuck in it with everybody else? Was that September morning the machine executing as written, or only men doing what men do? Are the things over Lake Huron and in a whistleblower's testimony the admins checking their logs, or weather balloons and wishful thinking? The manual doesn't say. The record doesn't say.

On Mount Hermon, where the old book says the admins first logged in, the snow still sits on a contested border, and every flag on its slopes belongs to someone who was told the mountain was theirs. The architecture is still running. Whether anyone is watching it is the one question left unanswered, and maybe the only one worth asking.

text:
At The Controls
Michel Talbot

HP 2116B Minicomputer
This 16-bit computer has been adapted as an automated circuit board test station for the HP9100 programmable calculator assembly line at the Hewlett-Packard Loveland Division in Colorado (September 1968).

The interface unit on the left is currently testing the Braid memory control logic board. The minicomputer was coupled to two 100 input scanners each with reed relay contacts capable of 200 scan points per second as well as a digital voltmeter and three programmable power supplies.
Use of a digital computer to control board testing offers a number of important advantages. Many tests may be performed in a short time and the test data stored in computer memory. The computer can analyze the test data and provide instantaneous printout of fault diagnostics. By using programmable power supplies, the actual operating margins may be measured and printed, thereby simulating adverse environments or detecting processing changes which may influence the performance range of the assembly. Test automation also assures that the test is repeated identically on a day to day run or run to run basis for greatest accuracy.
The HP 2116A was Hewlett-Packard's first computer introduced in 1966 and originally developed as an instrument controller but it was so versatile and inexpensive that many customers bought one for use as a standalone computer. This particular third generation Model B was built using integrated circuits and had 8192 words of core memory that was expandable to 32K words.
Tens of thousands of machines in the series were sold over its 25-year lifetime, making HP the fourth-largest minicomputer vendor.

text:
I get that, Anthony. For sure. 

I understand probability, and again, love your work. So this is just about the subject, nothing personal at all. 

I have to ask, though, in all sincerity...

Is it not a structural disadvantage that the Rockies have to play at altitude, causing them to have still not solved their faced-by-no-other-team pitching problems in their 35+ year existence?   

We could take $100 million from every team to relocate the Rockies and build them a new stadium someplace else. But should those other teams - who never forced the Rockies owners to put a team in Colorado - have to do that? If yes, how, now, to make the other 29 unfairly-put-upon MLB owners whole?   

Is it fair that the beautiful weather and relaxed media in San Diego be so much more appealing to stars with a multiple high offers than playing in New York is?   

Where do we stop with trying to neutralize every single disadvantage? Is there a principled difference between the unfairness of a free labor market and the unfairness of any number of other serious structural disadvantages one could name throughout MLB?

text:
"Web3 cannot exist without blockchain, but blockchain can exist without Web3"👀

"Blockchain" (Block + Chain) is simply a Tech that affords us store information in blocks that are connected in chain across various computers, hence "chain."

Web 3, on the other hand which has always been referred to as the next generation internet.

In the past, we've had Web 1.0 (which entails sites like Wikipedia, you can only consume information on the internet, but can not interact with it). 
Then we had Web 2.0, which came with the innovation of users being able to interact with the information they find there, such as making and engaging content there, e.g, Facebook, YouTube, etc. 

As beautiful as Web 1.0 and 2.0 was and is, they have their own limitations, and one of it is centralization.

They are centered on a particular body which has basically authority over your data, information, and whatever you put out there, they basically are the middleman between you and your target audience. 

Web3.0 came to solve that problem, it offered the public the benefit of decentralization, where you can have a direct link to your target audience without a middleman, affording you privacy. 

Now back to the topic, yes; Web3 cannot exist without blockchain because the Decentralization enjoyed here is only made possible by Blockchain Tech.

Blockchain literally predates even the Web3 space. This further backs the claim that Blockchain can exist without Web3, while Web3 can not see the light of the day without Blockchain Tech😊

text:
Warren Buffett watched 16 geniuses lose $4.6 billion in 1998, then explained it in 1 sentence.

October 15, 1998. A lecture hall at the University of Florida.

A 68-year-old Buffett takes a student question about Long-Term Capital Management. 22 days earlier, the fund had nearly taken Wall Street down with it.

LTCM had 2 Nobel laureates on board, Myron Scholes and Robert Merton. It returned 43% in year 2 and 41% in year 3.

At the start of 1998 it held $4.7 billion of its own money. And $124.5 billion of borrowed money.

25 to 1.

Then Russia defaulted in August. In under 4 months, $4.6 billion was gone.

On September 23, Buffett, AIG and Goldman Sachs offered $250 million for the partners’ stake plus $3.75 billion in fresh capital. He gave John Meriwether under 1 hour. The deadline passed. That same day, 14 banks put in $3.625 billion under the eye of the Fed.

On stage, Buffett didn’t mock them.

He said they had about as high an IQ as any 16 people working together in one business in the country. 300 to 400 years of combined experience. Most of their net worth sat inside the fund.

Then he said it:

“To make money they didn’t have and didn’t need, they risked what they did have and what they did need.”

He offered a gun with a million chambers and 1 bullet. His answer: “I would not pull the trigger.”

The smartest room in finance lost to 1 ratio. 25 to 1.

Personally feel like he’s been off to a strong start. I’m not going to pretend to know what other ADs did before him; I was way too young to understand even if I did pay attention to it. 

But now that I literally work in the business side of the sports industry (would take a role with UMD in a heartbeat if it were offered lol), I can confidently say I’m a fan of a lot of the moves and initiatives he’s started. 

Next Gen Terps is a great move - discounted Terrapin club for young alumni and fans… get us invested early at a less daunting price point. 

He’s talked about finding more ways to monetize our stadiums/arenas out of season. He has ambitions of building something similar to what the Braves have going on with their “campus” to make it a destination venue for visiting fans (taking our opponents money!!)

He’s committed to the game-day promotions and actually honing in on what makes people more likely to attend games beyond the product on the field (concourse improvements, overall gameday atmosphere, etc.) 

He’s doing a lot of the right things from a business perspective that don’t make headlines. That’s why I have more faith in him than I see most others. He’s done some great podcast appearances if you’re interested. 

I only have a hard time imagining other ADs have actually done stuff like that considering he’s been able to implement so many of these initiatives so fast. If they had been, there’d just be less for him to do, ya know?
